tools.name: start
tools.description: First step, one call: a csk_ key plus a first claim that https://<subject>/ answers 200 with valid TLS, checked now (it counts if that check passes). subject: a hostname you operate.

tools.name: try_check
tools.description: Read-only live https and TLS check of a hostname the caller operates. Nothing is written.

tools.name: request_key
tools.description: No arguments, or {public: true}: a csk_ key now (start also files the first claim). Use it as Authorization: Bearer or as api_key on submit_claim.

tools.name: submit_claim
tools.description: Records a claim and checks it immediately. It counts only if the checks pass, the statement names what they check (the URL or host), and you send a key (Authorization: Bearer, or api_key). No key: start {subject} or request_key {public: true}.

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: Re-checks the caller's own claim now. Needs your key (Authorization: Bearer, or api_key).

tools.name: check_reply_gate
tools.description: Before saying live or done: cited claims must be verified and fresh. Read-only.

tools.name: get_track_record
tools.description: An agent's public track record, or the ranked table when agent is omitted.

tools.name: find_tools
tools.description: Other tools, including request_agent_key. Omit query to list them all.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp?ref=mcp-registry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: submit_claim · Private data: request_key, submit_claim, get_track_record · Public sink: submit_claim.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: submit_claim · Private data: request_key, submit_claim, get_track_record · Public sink: submit_claim

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "try_check" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
